summary: Regression tests for the production 'edits revert' bug. Backend fixes are solid: object-storage-backed /api/upload works end-to-end (files not on local disk, served with correct content-type), PUT /api/site persists across `supervisorctl restart backend`, and GET /api/site deep-merges defaults so partial docs cannot blank out sections. HOWEVER, the FRONTEND fix described in the review request was NOT actually applied — AdminDashboard.jsx still seeds the editor from the hardcoded default site BEFORE /api/site finishes fetching, and Save then pushes those hardcoded defaults over the DB. This is the exact bug the user reported. Reproduced deterministically: injected marker values into DB via API (kicker='RACE_MARKER_KICKER', price='$77.77'), opened /admin/dashboard, form displayed the HARDCODED defaults ('Handmade · Volcanic · Intentional' and '$24.00/$28.00') instead of the DB values. Editing the kicker + Save then WIPED the DB back to hardcoded defaults (the $77.77 price was silently reverted to $24.00). DB restored after test.

ui_bugs.component: AdminDashboard.jsx (site editor seeding effect at lines 88-90)
ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL — race NOT fixed. Effect is `useEffect(() => { if (site && !data) setData(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(site))); }, [site, data]);` — it never checks `siteLoading`. Because SiteContext initializes `site` to a hardcoded `defaultSite` object (SiteContext.jsx line 61: `useState(defaultSite)`), `site` is TRUTHY on the very first render. The effect immediately clones defaultSite into `data`, THEN /api/site resolves and setSite is called — but the effect's `!data` guard now blocks any re-seed. Result: the editor form permanently shows hardcoded defaults, and Save PUTs those defaults over the real DB, silently reverting every field that had been customized to a non-default value. This is exactly the user-reported 'saves at first but reverts back' symptom. The FIX MUST be: `useEffect(() => { if (!siteLoading && site && !data) setData(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(site))); }, [site, siteLoading, data]);` (add the `!siteLoading` guard).

integration_issues.flow: Admin edit → Save → other fields revert
integration_issues.issue: Reproduced end-to-end via the deployed UI: (1) DB set to kicker='RACE_MARKER_KICKER', price='$77.77' via API; (2) Opened /admin/dashboard with valid admin JWT in localStorage; (3) Hero-kicker input rendered as 'Handmade · Volcanic · Intentional' and product prices as '$24.00'/'$28.00' — proving the form is seeded from hardcoded defaults, not the DB; (4) Edited kicker to 'EDITED_MARKER_KICKER'; (5) Clicked 'Save changes'; toast 'Saved' appeared; (6) After reload, kicker went back to 'Handmade · Volcanic · Intentional' (default) and price went back to '$24.00'. The Save request PUT the entire hardcoded default site to /api/site, wiping the DB customizations. Backend confirmed the DB actually contains the edited kicker briefly but the frontend re-seeds from defaults on every load, so the user sees 'saves at first but reverts back' — exactly the reported prod symptom.

action_items: CRITICAL — Fix AdminDashboard.jsx lines 88-90. Change `if (site && !data) setData(...)` to `if (!siteLoading && site && !data) setData(...)` and add `siteLoading` to the deps array. Without this, the entire object-storage/media-persistence/deep-merge chain of backend fixes is useless because the frontend keeps overwriting the DB with hardcoded defaults every time an admin saves anything. This is the ORIGINAL user-reported bug and it is STILL reproducible on the deployed preview.

OPTIONAL — Consider removing the `useState(defaultSite)` initial value in SiteContext.jsx (line 61) and using `useState(null)` instead, so that no consumer can accidentally read stale hardcoded values before the real fetch resolves. Downstream components would need a `if (loading) return null;` gate but this is a cleaner data-flow model.

OPTIONAL — After the AdminDashboard fix, add a data-testid on every form field (`hero-kicker-input`, `product-0-price-input`, `save-changes-btn`, `hero-section-toggle`, etc.) so this scenario can be regression-tested with stable selectors. Currently the test had to fall back to label/xpath queries.
critical_code_review_comments: SiteContext.jsx L61: `useState(defaultSite)` seeds every consumer with a huge hardcoded object BEFORE /api/site returns. This is the root cause of the race — any component that reads `site` synchronously on first render gets the hardcoded defaults, and if it then commits those to state (as AdminDashboard does) or PUTs them back, the DB is silently overwritten. Consider `useState(null)` + a `if (loading) return <Spinner/>` guard in the pages that need the data.

SiteContext.jsx L68: `setSite({ ...defaultSite, ...data })` shallow-merges only top-level keys. If the API returns `hero: { kicker: 'x' }` (partial), the shallow spread REPLACES `defaultSite.hero` wholesale, dropping mediaUrl / titleLine1 / etc. Should mirror the backend's `_deep_merge`. (Backend already deep-merges on GET so this may be moot today, but it's a latent hazard.)

AdminDashboard.jsx L88-90: uses `[site, data]` deps but never re-seeds after the initial fetch. If the admin uses the AI Writer or another tab writes to /site while the editor is open, `refresh()` will update `site` but `data` stays stale — a save from that stale `data` will silently roll back the other change. Consider re-seeding when a fresh `site` arrives (e.g., when `site` version/updatedAt changes) or at minimum surfacing a 'site changed on server, discard local edits?' banner.

server.py has grown to 2287 lines. The 2FA + password policy + 2FA-reset + admin-crud + upload + storage + site + media all live in one file. Overdue for a split (uploads.py, admin.py, admin_2fa.py, site.py).

server.py _storage_get: on a 403 it invalidates the cached storage_key and retries once — good — but any other transient error (5xx) is not retried. Object storage will occasionally 502; wrap the fetch in a retry-with-backoff (tenacity or a small loop) to avoid intermittent /api/uploads/<name> 502s from bubbling to users.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The backend fixes (object storage, deep-merge, PUT persistence across restart) are fully working — /app/backend/tests/test_site_and_uploads.py has 5 passing regression tests. The FRONTEND race bug in AdminDashboard.jsx is UNFIXED as of this iteration despite the review request claiming it was fixed. To reliably reproduce: PUT /api/site with a distinctive kicker/price via the minted admin JWT, then open /admin/dashboard in a browser — you'll see the form filled with hardcoded defaults from SiteContext, not the DB values. The one-line fix is in AdminDashboard.jsx L88: add `!siteLoading &&` to the guard and add `siteLoading` to the deps array on L90. After the fix, re-run the frontend flow: (a) inject marker into DB, (b) open dashboard, (c) verify form shows marker, (d) edit kicker, (e) reload, (f) verify kicker persisted AND price NOT reverted.
rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: SiteContext.jsx initializes `site` to a hardcoded `defaultSite` constant (L61), so `site` is truthy on the very first render — BEFORE /api/site resolves. AdminDashboard.jsx L88-90 seeds the editor's `data` state from `site` guarded only by `!data`, not by `!siteLoading`. Consequence: `data` is cloned from the hardcoded template, and the effect's `!data` guard prevents any re-seed when the real DB values arrive milliseconds later. When the admin clicks Save, the entire hardcoded template is PUT to /api/site, silently overwriting any customizations. REPRODUCTION: 1) `curl -X PUT /api/site` to set kicker='X', price='$77.77'. 2) Open /admin/dashboard with valid admin token. 3) Observe the Hero kicker input shows 'Handmade · Volcanic · Intentional' and the Product price shows '$24.00' — NOT the DB values. 4) Edit any field and Save. 5) Reload — every customization not in the hardcoded default is now gone. MITIGATION: One-line fix — add `!siteLoading` to the guard in AdminDashboard.jsx L88 and include `siteLoading` in the deps array. Optionally harden further by initializing SiteContext with `useState(null)` and gating consumers on `if (loading) return null;`.
